# What this design could detect {#sec-detection-floor}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("../_setup.R")
sc <- synth_counts(n_per_group = 4)
lib <- colSums(sc$counts)
logcpm <- log2(t(t(sc$counts + 1) / (lib + 1) * 1e6))
treated <- sc$samples$group == "treated"
n_per_group <- sum(treated)
pooled_sd <- sqrt((apply(logcpm[, treated], 1, var) + apply(logcpm[, !treated], 1, var)) / 2)
alpha <- report_param("fdr")
power <- report_param("power")
kept <- rowMeans(sc$counts) >= report_param("min_count")
mde <- ((qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) + qnorm(power)) * pooled_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group))[kept]
floor_df <- data.frame(mean_logcpm = rowMeans(logcpm)[kept], mde = mde)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## In plain terms
This chapter says how large a change had to be before this design could see it. Smaller changes may exist but would be missed.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Status
Last run on the synthetic example data, `r format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m-%d")`. Replace with your data source and date.
:::

**Question.** What is the smallest log2 fold change this design could detect, for a typical feature?

**Design.** `r n_per_group` samples per group. The minimum detectable effect is computed for each of the `r fmt(sum(kept))` features kept by the count filter, the same features that Results tests, from its pooled within-group standard deviation of log CPM. Nothing is tested.

The minimum detectable effect uses a two-sided normal approximation at alpha `r alpha` and power `r power`. It ignores the multiple-testing correction, so it is a lower bound on the true floor.

## Smallest detectable change {#sec-detection-floor-mde}

Example output on synthetic data. Replace with your analysis.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## How to read this
Each point is one feature. A point high on the y-axis is a feature whose change would have to be large before this design could see it. The dashed line is the median floor.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-detection-floor-mde
#| fig-cap: "Minimum detectable absolute log2 fold change per feature against mean log CPM, for every synthetic feature kept by the count filter. The dashed line marks the median floor."
#| fig-alt: "A scatter plot with one point per kept feature. The floor is highest for features with low mean log CPM and falls as the mean rises."
ggplot(floor_df, aes(mean_logcpm, mde)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, colour = HOUSE_PAL[["down"]]) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(floor_df$mde), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Mean log CPM", y = "Minimum detectable |log2 fold change|")
```

The median detection floor is `r round(median(mde), 2)` log2 units. For `r frac(sum(mde > report_param("lfc_threshold")), length(mde))` features, the floor is above the fold-change threshold of `r report_param("lfc_threshold")`.
